newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS - Euro markets firm ahead of U.S. rate decision.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - Euro markets firm ahead of U.S. rate decision.

text.p: European stocks and bonds rallied on Tuesday after investors on both sides of the Atlantic appeared to accept the idea that the U.S. Federal Reserve was set to raise interest rates for the first time in more than two years.
All three of Europe's major bourses -- London, Paris and Frankfurt -- rose strongly, while Wall Street built on Monday's 100.46 points in volatile early trading.

On the foreign exchange market the dollar eased from its highs against the yen by mid-afternoon and was drifting against the yen, although movements were small ahead of a policy-making meeting of the U.S. central bank.
German government bonds also firmed with British bonds or gilts, taking their cue from a rally in U.S. bonds overnight after the markets factored in a 0.25 percentage point rise in U.S. rates.
"A quarter-point rate rise is fully discounted now," said Norman Beauchamp, head of derivatives at the Cooperative Bank in London.
Investor focus stayed firmly on the Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC), which was due to announce the result of its deliberations after 1900 GMT, after the close of European markets.
"The case for a tightening (of credit) is a pretty good one," said Joel Prakken, chairman of Macroeconomic Advisers in the United States. "The chances of it are pretty high."
With financial markets primed for a rate increase, analysts said investors were now looking at the prospects for continuing U.S. economic expansion.
But until a decision emerges from the FOMC, one London dealer said he expected European markets to remain cautious.

Should the FOMC decide to raise rates by half a percentage point, share markets are likely to fall on both sides of the Atlantic. No rate increase could spark an initial, but short-lived rally, analysts said.
London blue chips, which fell 4.7 percent during the six sessions up until Monday, rebounded more than one percent.
By 1515 GMT, the benchmark index was up about 44 points at 4,259, just off the best levels of the day.

Among individual stocks, shares in Abbey National Plc rose 14.5p to 728.5 as bank stocks rallied from recent weakness and the market welcomed Abbey's failure to win control of insurer Scottish Amicable. Prudential Corp, confirmed as the winning bidder, rose 15.5p to 555.5 after being seen deriving strategic and earnings benefits from the deal
Shares in British Steel bucked the firmer market trend, sinking 3.5 pence to 158.125 after news that Germany's Krupp steel firm had called off its bid for Thyssen .
The shares of both German companies fell in Frankfurt trading, Krupp dropping 7.5 marks to 331 but well off its lows, while Thyssen plunged 42 marks to 375.5.
The blue chip DAX-30 index, supported by the firm dollar and bonds, closed floor trade just short of its high of the day with a 27.3 point gain to 3,349.14.
French shares were trading nearly one percent higher by mid-afternoon and above the key 2,600 level as the market advanced in line with other European bourses.
The blue-chip CAC-40 index was up 23 points or 0.92 percent at 2,602.93 at 1515 GMT.
With the foreign exchange market having priced in a 25-basis-point hike in the key Federal funds rate, there was little the dollar could do until the Fed actually made a move, traders said.

"A small rate hike is already priced in," said Hans Boman, chief spot dealer at Swedbank in New York. "We might see the dollar go up slowly after the announcement, but I don't think you'll see a major move in either direction."
CURRENCIES AT 1515 GMT
The dollar was quoted at 1.6894 marks and 123.68 yen compared with 1.6874 and 122.85 in late European trade on Monday.
STOCK MARKETS AT 1515 GMT
LONDON - The FTSE-100 index was up 41.0 points, or 0.97 percent, at 4,255.8.
PARIS - The CAC-40 was up 23.65 points, or 0.92 percent, at 2,602.93.
FRANKFURT - The 30-share DAX index closed floor trade up 27.3 points, or 0.82 percent, at 3,347.44. In later screen-based trade the IBIS DAX index was up 1.39 percent at 3,348.48.
PRECIOUS METALS

Platinum fixed at $374.75 versus $376.50 in the morning following news that unions at Russia's Norilsk Nickel had agreed not to disrupt output through June 30. Gold was down 10 cents at $350.65, while silver was two cents up at $5.16.
